::: {#def-significance-level}
#### Significance level

A hypothesis test with **significance level** $\siglevel$
rejects the [null hypothesis](#def-null-hypothesis)
when the [p-value](#def-p-value) is at most $\siglevel$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-significance-level-convention}
#### Choosing a significance level

$\siglevel = 0.05$ is a common convention, not a rule.
When $H_0$ is true and the p-value is computed exactly,
a test with significance level $\siglevel$ rejects $H_0$
with probability at most $\siglevel$;
for a test based on an approximate p-value, such as a large-sample test,
this holds only approximately.
:::
